metadata.title: Assessment of Rework, Its Causes and Impacts in RCC Building Construction Projects of Pokhara Metropolitan City

slides.title: Assessment of Rework, Its Causes and Impacts in RCC Building Construction Projects of Pokhara Metropolitan City
slides.subtitle: Final Report Presentation

slides.title: Presentation Outline
bullets: Background and research objectives
Literature review, study approach and field documentation
Waterproofing and threshold observations
Roof, masonry and plaster observations
Discussion, conclusions and recommendations

slides.title: Understanding Construction Rework
bullets: Rework involves correcting, removing or repeating work already executed.
A visible defect is a reason to investigate, not proof of completed rework.
Both the original work and the corrective intervention must be established.
Additional cost and time need separate, traceable records.

slides.title: Research Background
bullets: The study considers construction-quality concerns in RCC building work in Pokhara.
The main subjects are waterproofing and masonry/plaster workmanship.
Water ingress and cracking may have multiple explanations.
The aim is to describe what was observed before assigning a cause or consequence.

slides.title: Research Objectives
bullets: Document building-work concerns in waterproofing and masonry/plaster.
Discuss relevant construction mechanisms and technical requirements.
Identify the records needed to confirm actual corrective work.
Recommend practical inspections and rework-prevention measures.

slides.title: Study Scope and Evidence
bullets: Area of interest: Pokhara Metropolitan City.
Approach: qualitative construction-site observations and technical review.
Visual material: 17 building-work photographs in the current manuscript.
Road pavement and other non-building photographs are excluded.
The record does not support city-wide rework rates or financial totals.

slides.title: Methodology
bullets: Record construction concerns and the available field accounts.
Group observations by waterproofing or masonry/plaster work.
Read photographs descriptively before assessing possible mechanisms.
Compare with the project details, technical guidance and literature.
Separate suspected concerns from documented corrective events.

slides.title: When Is Rework Verified?
bullets: Observed concern: a condition visible on site or described in a field account.
Suspected case: identifiable earlier work and a possible subsequent correction.
Verified event: previous execution and corrective intervention both documented.
Measured impact: additional labour, materials, cost or time linked to that event.

rows.key_finding: Analysis of 788 incidents in Spanish building projects linked rework cost to initial contract value and company distance.
rows.project_relevance: Illustrates the need for case-level records; its cost model cannot estimate Pokhara project losses.

rows.key_finding: This review links rework reduction to error-management culture, leadership, and learning rather than cause lists alone.
rows.project_relevance: Supports prevention and reporting discussions without assigning an unverified local cause.

rows.key_finding: The authors identify early indicators of manageable rework causes and link them to preventive construction practices.
rows.project_relevance: Informs proposed pre-covering inspections for wet areas, masonry interfaces, and finish work.
rows.finding_locator: Publisher abstract, study aim and findings summary

rows.key_finding: The paper classifies rework causes across design, procurement and construction stages and assigns contract-party roles.
rows.project_relevance: Helps separate plausible source categories from causes proven in a particular Pokhara case.

rows.key_finding: The study identifies stakeholder coordination and site-worker training among important construction rework drivers.
rows.project_relevance: Provides comparative context for supervision; these rankings are not measurements from Pokhara.

rows.key_finding: In the Singapore sample, projects using BIM tended to report lower rework occurrence and impact.
rows.project_relevance: Supports better design review and documentation, not a claim of BIM use at the observed sites.

rows.key_finding: NBC 205:2024 is explicitly scoped to low-rise RC buildings without masonry infill.
rows.project_relevance: Check the actual building system and drawings before declaring any masonry-band provision applicable.
rows.finding_locator: DUDBC official NBC 205:2024 title/scope and building-code catalogue

rows.key_finding: HYDRO BAN installation instructions specify compatible drain, penetration and movement-joint treatments.
rows.project_relevance: Guides comparison of wet-area details; applicability depends on the specified product, not every membrane.
rows.finding_locator: HYDRO BAN installation instructions, drains/penetrations and movement joints

slides.title: Waterproofing: Main Concerns
bullets: Continuity at wet-area floors, corners, drains and pipe penetrations.
Transition details at door thresholds and adjoining walls.
Roof falls, parapet interfaces, outlets and possible moisture paths.
Compatibility of waterproofing layers with later tile, screed or plaster work.

slides.title: Lamachur Door Threshold
bullets: The field account describes leakage near a residential-house door threshold.
It also describes exposure, correction and reinstatement near the threshold.
The photographs show construction stages but do not verify every date or cause.
Costs, quantities and delay were not established in the current manuscript.

slides.title: Waterproofing: What Must Be Checked?
bullets: Identify the actual source of water: membrane, drainage, plumbing or another path.
Inspect membrane upstands, corners, penetrations and substrate preparation.
Use system-specific installation instructions and appropriate water testing.
Document the original detail and the corrective work before counting rework.

slides.title: Other Roof and Finish Observations
bullets: Separate images show a stair finish, parapet surfaces, roof edges and capping.
Discoloration and surface marks do not establish a single leakage mechanism.
These photographs come from different conditions, not one confirmed event.
Drawings, drainage details and site inspection are needed for diagnosis.

slides.title: Masonry and Plaster Workmanship
bullets: Wall junctions require examination of intended bonding or connector details.
Cracks near intersections may have more than one possible cause.
Brick absorption, mortar preparation, curing and substrate conditions matter.
Concealed sill/lintel details cannot be confirmed from external marks alone.

slides.title: Interpreting Plaster Cracks
bullets: Check whether the wall junction is bonded, butted or joined with designed ties.
Review drawings and applicable code requirements for openings and bands.
Investigate movement, material preparation, plaster thickness and curing.
Avoid selecting a cosmetic repair before identifying the likely mechanism.

slides.title: Comparison of the Two Work Categories
bullets: Waterproofing: verify membrane continuity, drainage paths and transitions.
Masonry/plaster: verify connection details, materials and curing.
In both, appearance alone does not establish cause or cost.
Inspection before concealment can help reveal workmanship concerns.

slides.title: Recommendations: Waterproofing
bullets: Check wet-area and terrace details against approved designs.
Inspect the substrate and continuity at corners, thresholds and penetrations.
Use compatible product systems and required tests before covering finishes.
Keep dated inspection, repair and reinstatement records.
slides.recommendation_basis: Manuscript v1.12 Chapter 5 and active technical bibliography

slides.title: Recommendations: Masonry and Plaster
bullets: Inspect intersecting wall connections against the approved drawings.
Verify required opening reinforcement for the actual building type.
Check brick condition, mortar preparation, curing and plaster substrate.
Investigate recurring cracks before covering or replacing finishes.
slides.recommendation_basis: Manuscript v1.12 Chapter 5 and active technical bibliography

slides.title: Study Limitations
bullets: This is a qualitative discussion based on selected field accounts and photographs.
The 17 images are not a representative sample of Pokhara building projects.
Site records have not been fully matched to every photographed condition.
No verified city-wide event count, cost estimate or project delay is claimed.

slides.title: Conclusions
bullets: The reviewed field material illustrates practical waterproofing and masonry concerns.
Technical causes require site-specific inspection, drawings and, where needed, tests.
Documentation must link earlier work to any claimed corrective intervention.
Quality checks before finishing and reliable site records remain important.
